report.verdict: A marketing manager with strong lifecycle results, hidden behind a generic headline and About.
write_up: You run lifecycle marketing for a camping gear brand and manage a team and paid social budget. A recruiter has enough to start a conversation, but your headline and About don't show the work as well as the Fernhill job does.
The welcome series is your model: you say what you rebuilt and how the first-purchase rate changed. That result is already in your current job, ready to bring into your About.
Start with the headline and About, then fill in what you supported at Lumen Street. A recruiter looking for lifecycle marketing can connect your current work to a result without hunting for it.

cards.line: Marketing Manager | Storyteller | Growth Mindset | Lifelong Learner
cards.cannot_tell: 'Storyteller | Growth Mindset | Lifelong Learner' leaves out the lifecycle email and SMS work you do. Keep the personality and put that specialty beside your title.
cards.example: Marketing Manager | Lifecycle Email and SMS | Storyteller | Growth Mindset | Lifelong Learner
cards.question: What kind of lifecycle campaigns do you run besides the welcome series?

cards.line: Results-driven marketing professional with 8+ years of experience driving growth across multiple channels. Passionate about building brands people love and leading high-performing teams.
cards.cannot_tell: 'Results-driven' could describe almost anyone in marketing. Your welcome series tells a recruiter what you changed and what happened next.
cards.example: I run lifecycle email and SMS for a direct-to-consumer camping gear brand with 410,000 subscribers. I rebuilt the welcome series from 3 emails to 7, which raised first-purchase rate from 4.2% to 6.8% over two quarters.
cards.question: What did you change in the welcome series besides the number of emails?

cards.line: Rebuilt the welcome series from 3 emails to 7, which raised first-purchase rate from 4.2% to 6.8% over two quarters.
cards.cannot_tell: This is the line to copy the rest after. It names the series, your change and the first-purchase rate before and after.

cards.line: Supported client accounts and helped with reporting.
cards.cannot_tell: 'Supported' and 'helped' leave the client work hidden. Which accounts did you work on, and what reporting did you help produce?
cards.example: Supported [number] client accounts and helped with [which reports] for [which clients].
cards.question: Which client accounts did you support, how many were there, and what reports did you help produce?

cards.cannot_tell: Leadership doesn't name the marketing work your current job describes. Lifecycle email, SMS and paid social give a recruiter more useful skills to filter by.
cards.question: Which of lifecycle email, SMS and paid social are central to your current work?

fit.why: Your headline and current title name you as a Marketing Manager, and your Fernhill work centers on lifecycle email, SMS and paid social.
fit.level: manager, your title and management of two marketing specialists
fit.note: 'Marketing Manager' is in your headline and current title. 'lifecycle email' and 'SMS' are in your current job, while 'Klaviyo' is in your earlier Fernhill job. Someone hiring for this work may also search for segmentation, A/B testing and retention marketing; none appears on your profile. Add segmentation and A/B testing to your current job description and retention marketing to your About only if they describe your work. Bring lifecycle email into your headline first.
